How to install Linux Mint on your Windows PC | ZDNet

I think Linux Mint isn't just a great desktop, it's a great replacement for Windows.

It is definitely a valid replacement. Still not there yet, the typical Linux developer mentality is still too much focused on showing off his cool console tricks to fix things, but Mint is coming very close to what Windows users are used to.

"Software manager" is basically a point an click way to install applications easily. And even better to also "uninstall". I also found that you could uninstall right clicking the icon.

There is a driver update icon, control panel that looks similar to what you are used to in Windows. And a shield icon that turns out to be an Linux updater that makes updating as easy as updating windows. Pure mouse clicks.

Adding user is also very simple. again mouse clicks as you would expect in Windows.

Microsoft Office replacement, WPS office is the closes one that has the "professional" feel.

Icons on the task bar just like Windows, but I still have not figured out to have shortcuts for my desktop. I can find the application by pressing the "start" menu, but that is too much mouse clicks, I would love to have a shortcut on the desktop by dragging it to my desktop with §the right mouse button.

Something I really miss is a functioning mouse button to surf the web pages (Firefox) back space. Now I have to press the back space. This tales more energy.

The big concern I have is when Mint 18.0 comes out. It is now 17.3 and what happens when I do "upgrade". Does it destroy my current Linux or does it safely upgrade my version. As a company I would not want to risk reinstalling Mint again because that is productivity loss.
